previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and end-stage renal disease status post left renal transplant was admitted for progressive fatigue, lower extremity edema, nausea, diarrhea, and worsening kidney function. Initial evaluation revealed acute on chronic renal failure with elevated creatinine and microcytic anemia. Renal ultrasound showed no obstruction or abnormalities in the transplanted kidney. The patient received two units of packed red blood cells and IV fluids, with improvement in hemoglobin and symptoms. His antihypertensive regimen was adjusted due to renal dysfunction, including discontinuation of valsartan and transition to metoprolol and nifedipine, with addition of furosemide. Tacrolimus dose was reduced due to high trough levels, and calcitriol was initiated for secondary hyperparathyroidism. Diarrhea and nausea resolved with supportive care. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged for blood pressure and kidney function monitoring.

A/P: Pt is a ___ yo M with a PMH of type 2 DM, ESRD, s/p living

1) Hypertensive Urgency - On presentation, patient had BPs up to 
220s systolically requiring labetalol and ntg gtt, in the 
setting of being unable to tolerate PO medications for several 
days. The drips were subsequently weaned off overnight in the 
ICU and by hospital day 2, he was tolerating pos without 
difficulty. He was then transferred to the medical floor where 
his home-HTN regimen was restarted. The patient had occasional 
elevations of his SBPs to the 180s, occasionally associated with 
headaches, which responded to po medications and an uptitration 
of his prior doxazosin dose from 1 mg to 2 mg qhs. Given his 
progressive renal disease, the decision was made to start HD 
during this admission (see below). If his BPs remain elevated as 
an outpatient, addition of an ACE-I for angiotensin pathway 
blockade should be considered given known proximal renal artery 
stenosis on a renal ultrasound on admission.
.

appetite, likely due to uremia in the setting of rising 
creatinine.  Onset of emesis and diarrhea over past 2 days may 
have been due to superimposed gastroenteritis. Symptoms rapidly 
resolved upon admission. 
.
3) ESRD s/p failing living related donor transplant - Renal team 
consulted for possible initiation of HD. Given graft failure, 
uremic symptoms, and HTN urgency, the decision was made to 
initiate HD during this admission. The patient underwent a 
tunneled HD line placement by ___ on hospital day 1 without 
complication and HD was initiated on HD 2. He tolerated 3 
sessions of HD without complication. Epogen and calcitriol were 
switched to be given at HD. Cellcept was discontinued at the 
recommendation of the renal team. He will continue on prednisone 
and tacrolimus as well as phoslo. A PPD was negative. He will 
continue to receive HD as an outpatient at ___ q ___, 
and ___ followed by placement at ___ dialysis on ___.

4) Anemia  Likely due to ESRD, chronic disease, with possible 
contribution from immunosuppressive meds.  Hematocrit stable 
during admission. Received epogen at HD.

insulin at home. Placed on ISS. He will need to f/u with his PCP

radiology_notes.text:
RENAL TRANSPLANT ULTRASOUND

INDICATION:  Recent failure of renal transplant and abdominal pain with
nausea, vomiting, ? edema.

COMPARISON:  ___.

RENAL TRANSPLANT ULTRASOUND:  Gray-scale appearance of the transplant has not
changed though size is slightly larger measuring 12.4 cm today (11.4 cm on
prior). There is no hydronephrosis, mass, or stone.  There is no perinephric
fluid.

The main renal vein is patent. Main renal artery and upper, mid and lower pole
arteries demonstrate a new tardus parvus waveform, concerning for proximal
renal artery stenosis. The resistive indices of 0.76, 0.79, and 0.76 in the
upper, mid, and lower poles, compared to prior measurement of 0.72, 0.78, and
0.71. 

IMPRESSION:

Tardus parvus waveforms in the renal arteries, concerning for proximal renal
artery stenosis. This finding is new since prior study. Minimal elevation in
the resistive indices.

Findings were discussed with ___ MD (___) on the
day of the study.

PORTABLE AP CHEST

INDICATION:  Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, setting of diabetes, renal
transplant, and epigastric pain.

COMPARISON : ___.

FINDINGS: The lungs are clear without evidence of pneumonia. There is no
pneumothorax, pleural effusion.  The heart is enlarged without evidence of
CHF. The mediastinal silhouette is normal.  The osseous structures are
unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  Mild cardiomegaly, without CHF or acute intrathoracic process.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  ___ male with end-stage renal disease, requires
hemodialysis catheter placement.  Request is made for tunneled hemodialysis
catheter.

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___ and Dr. ___ was attending physician
and present for the entire procedure.

SEDATION:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of a
total of 50 mcg of fentanyl and 1 mg of Versed throughout the total
intraservice time of 22 minutes during which the patient's hemodynamic
parameters were continuously monitored.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  The patient was brought to the angiography suite and
placed supine on the imaging table.  The right neck was prepped and draped in
the usual sterile fashion.  Ultrasound guidance was used to access the right
internal jugular vein with a micropuncture needle through which an 0.018 wire
was passed using flouroscopic guidance.  Hard copy ultrasound images were
obtained before and after access.  The inner stiffener and wire were removed
and replaced with a short ___ wire.  Next, a subcutaneous tunnel was created
on the right upper anterior chest wall, through which the hemodynamic
hemodialysis catheter was pulled.  A peel-away sheath was placed over the
wire.  The wire and dilator were removed and the hemodialysis catheter was fed
through the sheath as the sheath was peeled away.  The final position of the
tip of the catheter is in the right atrium.  The length of the catheter is 23
cm tip to cuff.

Both ports flushed and aspirated easily.  Catheter was sutured to the skin and
a sterile dressing was applied.  There were no immediate complications.

IMPRESSION:  23 cm 15.5 ___ angiodynamics hemodialysis catheter placed via
the right internal jugular vein with tip in the right atrium. Ready for use.

VENOUS ULTRASOUND

INDICATION:  End-stage renal disease, evaluation for hemodialysis fistula
placement.

FINDINGS:

RIGHT ARM:  The basilic vein is patent, measuring 0.21 cm at the elbow, and
mid humerus and 0.27 cm at the level of the upper humerus.  The cephalic vein
is patent, measuring 0.16 cm above the wrist, 0.15 cm at the elbow and 0.15 cm
at the shoulder.

LEFT ARM:  The basilic vein is patent, measuring 0.24 cm at the elbow, 0.33 cm
at the level of the mid humerus and 0.37 cm at the level of the upper humerus.
The cephalic vein is patent, measuring 0.18 cm at the forearm and 0.17 cm at
the level of the elbow and the distal humerus.  From this level centrally the
vein is not clearly identified.  The subclavian veins are patent.  There is
triphasic flow in the single brachial artery on each side.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Patent right basilic and cephalic veins with the measurements as above.

2.  Patent left basilic vein with the measurements as above.

3.  Patent left cephalic vein from the wrist to the elbow and not visualized
from the elbow centrally.

microbiology.comments: NEGATIVE FOR CMV IgM ANTIBODY BY EIA.  INTERPRETATION:  INFECTION AT UNDETERMINED TIME.  A positive IgG result generally indicates past exposure.  Infection with CMV once contracted remains latent and may reactivate when immunity is compromised.  If current infection is suspected, submit follow-up serum in 2-3 weeks.  Greatly elevated serum protein with IgG levels >2000 mg/dl may cause  interference with CMV IgM results.
